evidence.question: Is the dividend safe?
evidence.text: Short answer: the data shows a dividend that has been raised modestly and is currently covered by earnings, funded alongside a low-leverage balance sheet — but the large "performance-linked" top-up that made 2024 payouts much bigger is gone, so the total cash per share is now well below its 2024 peak DB. Whether it stays that way depends on earnings the database does not forecast.What the dividend record shows- The quarterly base rate went SAR 0.33 → SAR 0.34 per share: the three quarters of 2025 (ex-dates 2025-05-21, 2025-08-19, 2025-11-17) paid 0.33, and the most recent three (ex-dates 2026-03-16, 2026-06-01, 2026-08-19) paid 0.34, each announced on schedule DB.- Cash paid per quarter rose from SAR 80,100–80,120 million in the four quarters through Q3_2025 to SAR 82,060–82,080 million in 2026 DB.- The cut is in the extras: Q1–Q3 2024 (SAR 40,410 million, SAR 40,390 million, SAR 40,390 million) carried large performance-linked dividends, and each 2024/2025 quarter note shows only SAR 820 million of performance-linked content; the 2026 quarters carry no performance-linked note at all DB. Those quarters paid SAR 116,450–116,510 million each versus roughly SAR 82,000 million now DB.Coverage and balance-sheet support- Trailing twelve-month EPS is SAR 1.84 against roughly SAR 1.35 of dividends declared over the last four ex-dates (0.34 + 0.34 + 0.34 + 0.33), an implied payout of about 73% of earnings DB. The database's own payout metric is not available (inputs missing), so that figure is only this arithmetic DB.- Profitability is high: ROE 26.75% and ROA 15.86% DB. The AlphaCouncil quality seat is bullish on ROE above 20%, and its income seat is bullish on a dividend yield above 5% (5.23%) DB.- Financial health scores 61.35 on the two published inputs: debt/equity 0.2006 (54th sector percentile) and current ratio 1.9986 (68.7th percentile) DB. Interest coverage and free-cash-flow yield are not published for this name, so cash-based coverage cannot be checked here DB.- The company has kept issuing debt in the period — a $4 billion bond close on 2026-02-02, a $3 billion sukuk on 2025-09-17 and $5 billion of bonds on 2025-06-01 — mostly for general corporate purposes, and on 2026-03-09 the board approved a buyback of up to 350 million shares for about SAR 11.3 billion from internal funds, small next to ~SAR 82 billion a quarter of dividends DB.The caution in the numbers- Price data undercuts the income story: the shares are down 0.94% over 1 month, 5.81% over 3 months and 7.60% over 6 months, sit 8.87% below their 52-week high, trade below both the 50-day (25.922) and 200-day (26.2878) averages, and the worst drawdown in the recorded range is 40.14% P1Key metrics.- The news and disclosure feed for this ticker is stale (last item 2026-03-09), so nothing here shows a dividend decision made after that date, and there is no analyst or guidance data in this terminal to project earnings forward P1Key metrics.So the visible support is: consecutive on-time declarations, a base-rate increase, earnings that covered the payout at ~73%, and low leverage. The visible strain is: earnings that have slipped (P/E 13.86 on TTM EPS 1.84 with a 6-month price decline), the withdrawal of the performance-linked uplift, and the absence of cash-flow and interest-coverage inputs to test coverage more strictly DB.Saudi Aramco (2222) — dividend history, SAR per shareget_dividends(2222)Pin to dashboardQuarterEx-datePay dateDPS (SAR)Amount (SAR mn)Q2_20262026-08-192026-08-270.3482,060Q1_20262026-06-012026-06-090.3482,080Q4_20252026-03-162026-03-310.3482,080Q3_20252025-11-172025-11-260.3380,120Q2_20252025-08-192025-08-280.3380,110Q1_20252025-05-212025-05-290.3380,110Q4_20242025-03-172025-03-260.3380,100Q3_20242024-11-142024-11-260.48116,450Q2_20242024-08-202024-08-290.48116,450Q1_20242024-05-142024-05-230.48116,510
